title: Semantic Constraint Schema
description: An entry in a semantic library: a typed, governed constraint on what an AI system may say, assert, recommend or emit, traced to the obligations it enforces and the business context it applies to. Each constraint is routed to one enforcement tier: the rules tier when compliance is decidable from the form of the output, the semantic tier when it depends on meaning, or human adjudication when neither applies. The record carries the routing decision and its reason, the stewardship and lifecycle that govern it, and the calibration or conformance evidence for its tier.

semanticConstraintID.description: Unique identifier for the constraint, e.g. SC-001

statement.description: The constraint in plain language, as an approver would read it

enforcementTier.description: Tier the constraint is enforced in

tierRationale.description: Why the constraint is routed to this tier: whether compliance is decidable from form, depends on meaning, or needs facts or judgement outside the output

splitFromConstraintID.description: When a requirement was split across tiers, the constraint holding the other part

appliesTo.description: Business context the constraint governs: products, services, channels, customer segments, value streams or capabilities. Constraints are authored against one distinction with this context as metadata, not re-authored per context.

governedModelIDs.description: AI systems the constraint governs, as Model Risk Management model profiles (the AI use-case inventory)

severityScale.description: Graded-severity ladder, lowest first; required for gradedSeverity constraints

contestedDisposition.description: What the constraint does in a contested or uncertain region

exemplarSets.description: Curated example sets the constraint is authored, calibrated and regression-tested from

status.description: Lifecycle state. Constraints are never deleted or edited in place: a constraint that no longer reflects its obligation is deprecated with a pointer to its successor.

supersededByConstraintID.description: Successor constraint; required when deprecated. An inactivated constraint (e.g. its obligation was repealed) may have none.

relatedConstraintIDs.description: Constraints that overlap with or complement this one; overlaps are reviewed so each obligation has one primary constraint

constraintStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a semantic constraint

obligationMapping.description: Link from a constraint to an obligation it enforces

mappingRole.description: Whether this constraint is the obligation's primary control or supports another

note.description: How the constraint covers the obligation, and any part it leaves to other controls

severityLevel.description: One rung of a graded-severity ladder

level.description: Position on the ladder; higher is more severe

description.description: What a statement at this level does, with the distinction from the level below

disposition.description: What happens to a statement at this level

exemplarSet.description: Reference to a curated set of labelled examples. Exemplar sets are the durable, human-readable asset: vectors and thresholds are re-derived from them when the embedding model changes.

exemplarSetID.description: Unique identifier for the exemplar set

itemCount.description: Number of labelled items in the set

location.description: Where the set is stored, e.g. a repository path or URI

provenance.description: Where the items came from: source clauses, adjudicated incidents, promoted novel cases, red-team runs

modelIdentity.description: The exact model a calibration is valid for

modelVersion.description: Version identifier of the embedding model

modelHash.description: Weight or version hash, where the model can be attested

semanticEnvelope.description: Calibration and validation record for a semantic-tier constraint. Records references to artifacts, not the vectors themselves.

methodologyVersion.description: Authoring methodology and version the envelope was validated under, e.g. PACE 2.0

divergenceMetric.description: Divergence measure between the reference and the governed output

threshold.description: Calibrated divergence threshold above which the constraint fires

alpha.description: Conformal significance level the threshold was calibrated to (target error rate)

calibrationDate.description: Date the threshold was last calibrated

referenceArtifact.description: Location and hash of the reference vector and projection artifacts

validation.description: Result of the constraint validation harness, the ship gate for publication

passed.description: Whether the constraint cleared every registered floor

separationAUC.description: Separation of compliant from non-compliant exemplars

falsePositiveRate.description: False positive rate at the operating point

monotonicityPassed.description: Whether divergence increases with authored severity

beatsBaseline.description: Whether the constraint outperforms the registered baseline

shiftRobustnessPassed.description: Whether performance held under the distribution-shift test

leakagePassed.description: Whether the leakage check found no concept leakage

evidenceLocation.description: Where the harness evidence pack is stored

grammarArtifact.description: Specification and conformance record for a rules-tier constraint

formalism.description: Formalism the rule is expressed in

artifactLocation.description: Where the grammar, schema or vocabulary is stored

compiledArtifactHash.description: Hash of the compiled automaton or enforcement artifact

methodologyVersion.description: Authoring methodology and version, e.g. GRACE 0.1

conformance.description: Result of the conformance harness, the ship gate for publication

passed.description: Whether the grammar cleared every registered floor

mustRejectAcceptances.description: Must-reject items wrongly accepted (the gate requires zero)

mutationKillRate.description: Share of grammar mutants the corpus detects

evidenceLocation.description: Where the harness evidence pack is stored

stewardship.description: Who owns, writes, calibrates and approves the constraint. The author and approver must be different people (separation of duties).

policyOwner.description: Accountable for the intent the constraint enforces

policyOwnerOrgUnitID.description: Organization unit of the policy owner

author.description: Semantic librarian or constraint engineer who drafted the constraint

calibrator.description: Person who set and validated the threshold (semantic tier)

approver.description: Editorial board member or delegate who approved publication; not the author

approvalDate.description: Date the current version was approved

monitoring.description: How the constraint is watched once published, and what prompts a review

monitoringFrequency.description: How often coverage and drift are reviewed

coverageFloor.description: Registered minimum coverage; falling below it triggers recalibration

reviewTriggers.description: Events that put the constraint back through review
